remake.edit_prompt: Edit this video. Change ONLY these things and keep absolutely everything else exactly as it is (bodies, clothes, every movement and its timing, camera, background, lights): FIELD SHOT: 1) the hammer-throw athlete (royal-blue tank top, black shorts) becomes the Shiba Inu from image 1: Shiba head, and every bare arm, hand, leg and foot becomes a thick furry Shiba leg with a round paw; 2) each official in a lime-green shirt becomes a real dog of a different breed wearing the same lime-green shirt. STAGE SHOT: 3) the white fluffy singer in the black tuxedo and white bow tie becomes the same Shiba Inu from image 1 (Shiba head and fur, same tuxedo, same microphones, same black stage), its mouth opening and closing exactly like the original singer's mouth. Every replaced head is the Shiba Inu from image 1. Every visible arm, leg, hand and foot becomes a thick, fully furry orange-and-cream Shiba leg ending in a round Shiba paw (sleeves and trousers stay as they are). SAME HEADCOUNT: the number of animals in every frame matches the number of people in the original frame - one person becomes exactly one animal, never two. Body parts of a person seen at the frame edges belong to that same animal and stay attached to it. Remove any watermark or on-screen text. COMPOSITING QUALITY: the dog parts must look filmed in the same shot - match the original lighting direction, colour, shadows, motion blur, focus and film grain; the head is a natural size for the body and turns, nods and moves its mouth exactly with the original head motion; the fur blends seamlessly into the neck and collar and into the sleeves and trouser hems with no visible seam, outline or halo; the same dog in every frame with no flicker, morphing or changing markings. KEEP THESE MOMENTS EXACTLY AS IN THE VIDEO (the joke lives here): [1.0-2.0s] the throw goes wrong - the athlete spins and releases the hammer off-target, stumbling forward; [2.0-2.5s] the official gets hit - the hammer strikes the official on the bottom and the official doubles over in pain; [2.5-3.5s] the opera reaction - hard cut to the tuxedo singer opening its mouth wide on a dramatic high opera note, mouth exactly in sync with; [3.5-6.5s] the Queen of the Night ah-ah-ah run - the singer's mouth opens and closes sharply on every staccato note of the coloratura run, exactly like the ori.

copy_place.why: The top band covers the dog's head, ears, and face, whereas the bottom band is mostly open grass with ample clear space.

all.action: The athlete in a royal-blue tank top and black shorts stands in the throwing circle and begins the windup, holding the hammer wire; an official in a lime-green shirt stands to the right holding a clip
The athlete rotates hips and swings the hammer back with the right arm; the official watches.
The athlete spins forward across the circle and swings the arm forward, releasing the hammer off-target to the right.
The hammer flies straight toward the official; the athlete stumbles forward completing the release.
The hammer strikes the standing official on the bottom; the official doubles over and recoils in pain.
all.sound: impact thud and a spectator shout

all.action: CUT to a white fluffy dog in a black tuxedo and white bow tie, centered behind two microphones on stands, black stage; it opens its mouth wide and the high opera note begins.
The singer holds the long high note, head tilted slightly back.
The singer launches into the Queen of the Night staccato run: the mouth opens and closes sharply on each note.
all.mouth: opening and closing fast, one shape per note

all.action: Staccato run continues, head bobbing slightly with each note.
The run climbs to the top note and holds.
